source.title: A Spectral Theory of Grokking: Weight Decay induces Feature Learning
source.authors: Lenz Pracher; Pascal de Jong; Oskar Lieshaus; Alan Jeffares; S. Rulands

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a frozen-kernel stability condition, citing Cohen et al. (2021), to help interpret its optimizer-plane boundary. Its own experiments concern grokking on modular addition, not the claim versions’ stated behaviors and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-fit and no-fitting outcomes across learning-rate and weight-decay grids on modular addition. These results concern training fit but do not test a listed version in its stated setting. The discussion of the edge-of-stability condition is used to calibrate a boundary; the reported result is not a test of recovery from above the stability limit.
record.test_reason: The study uses a frozen-kernel stability condition to interpret its grokking phase boundary. It does not measure recovery above an independently measured initial stability limit, loss–curvature dynamics, or sustained edge-of-stability training. Its modular-addition MLP and Transformer experiments do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive a finite post-fit residual under homogeneous squared-loss dynamics with coupled weight decay, then connect it to task-aligned NTK growth through a reduced model with explicit coupling and mode-decoupling assumptions. Modular-addition experiments show post-fit NTK organization, optimizer-plane phase structure, and inverse learning-rate–decay transition-time scaling consistent with this account; the Transformer reproduces the macroscopic patterns.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines grokking on modular addition with MSE and coupled weight decay, not the classification benchmarks or interventions in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-fit and generalization outcomes vary across the learning-rate and weight-decay grids; the paper reports failure at stronger decay or large learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Modular-addition MLP and Transformer sweeps exhibit memorization, grokking, forgetting, and fitting failure as learning rate and coupled weight decay vary. One MLP run falls from peak training accuracy 0.948 to final accuracy 0.204.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate and coupled weight decay determine whether these modular-addition models reach and retain a 90% training-accuracy threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: The MLP training-fit boundary is summarized by a calibrated decay cutoff of 8.3821151 × 10−4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An effective decay cutoff summarizes training-fit failure in this particular modular-addition sweep.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code will be made publicly available upon publication)
record.problems: The phase sweeps use model seed 0 at every grid point; the paper gives no counts per phase category in the supplied text. The MLP boundary calibration uses effective coordinates inferred from the optimizer-plane boundary rather than direct measurements of NTK growth.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports NTK diagnostics, a temporary NTK-alignment intervention, held-out accuracy and MSE, and transition-time scaling. These do not measure a behavior named by the claim versions, so they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and the stated smaller-model and training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Comparative effects of activation-matched, Gaussian, and orthogonal initialization on training speed and trainable depth. Using He-normal initialization does not test these effects.

Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, the accompanying loss rise and curvature drop, larger-rate divergence relative to that limit, sharpness hovering at the stability threshold, and divergence from below it.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The stability overlay is calibrated to the observed boundary rather than computed from a directly measured NTK maximum eigenvalue. Neither this calibration nor the frozen-kernel derivation tests V5's nonlinear recovery or sharpness dynamics. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a verdict on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and varying student width relative to teacher width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, batch normalization comparisons, and the cited special-initialization and Fixup conditions.
Activation-matched or orthogonal initializations and their effects on learning speed or trainable depth.

Recovery from learning rates above an initial stability limit, the loss-rise/curvature-drop sequence, and sharpness hovering at a stability threshold. The paper reports optimizer-plane outcomes, but does not test those dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: bias-free 46 → 256 → 23 one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained an 84 × 90 learning-rate and weight-decay grid for 24,000 updates; categorized outcomes using 90% training and held-out accuracy thresholds.

conditions.value: 84 learning rates from 0.1 to 100 and 90 weight decays from 5 × 10−6 to 2 × 10−3

rows.measure: Training-fit outcome category across the grid
rows.value: The paper reports memorizing, grokking, forgetting, and no-fitting regions. Grokking requires final training and held-out accuracy above 90%; memorization requires final training accuracy above 90% and held-out accuracy below 90%; forgetting means training accuracy crossed 90% earlier but ends below it.
rows.note: This is an aggregate grid result on modular addition. The text does not give counts per outcome category.
rows.check: The phase summary combines different training outcomes in a modular-addition MLP; it does not measure any listed version. The 90% classification threshold does not establish near-zero training error.

rows.subject: one-block Transformer
rows.size_stated: one block; dmodel = 32; four attention heads; feed-forward width 64
rows.stage_stated: trained; model seed 0 at every grid point
rows.operation_detail: Trained a 42 × 45 learning-rate and weight-decay grid for 60,000 updates; categorized outcomes using 90% phase definitions.

conditions.value: 42 learning rates from 5 × 10−3 to 103 and 45 weight decays from 10−7 to 10−3
MSE between softmax probabilities and one-hot targets

rows.measure: Training-fit outcome category across the grid
rows.value: The paper reports a weak-decay memorization region, an intermediate grokking band, and failure at stronger decay or large learning rate. It uses the same 90% phase definitions as for the MLP.
rows.note: The text describes the aggregate phase structure but does not give counts per outcome category.
rows.check: The Transformer phase summary does not measure any listed version. Large-learning-rate failure alone does not establish V5 without a measured stability threshold and the relevant training dynamics.

rows.subject: bias-free 46 → 256 → 23 one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained a representative fixed grid cell and reported its training accuracy peak and final value.
rows.value: The forgetting example reaches peak training accuracy 0.948 and ends at 0.204.
rows.note: The paper classifies this run as forgetting because training accuracy crossed 90% earlier but ends below it.
rows.check: The reported peak accuracy of 0.948 and final accuracy of 0.204 are correct, but this modular-addition MLP does not test V1's convolutional-network claim. Its forgetting outcome cannot be assigned a partial state against an unlinked version.

rows.subject: bias-free 46 → 256 → 23 one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Calibrated an effective training-fit cutoff on the optimizer-plane grid.
rows.measure: Effective weight-decay cutoff for training fit
rows.note: This is a calibrated boundary location, not a reported training-accuracy value for an individual run.
rows.check: Remove as a behavioral result row: 8.3821151 × 10−4 is a fitted boundary parameter selected to minimize final-training-accuracy misclassification, rather than a measured training outcome or an independently tested stability limit.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
